title: Three fresh sealed sets, pinned before any run: Home v2, the conversation v3 and the journeys v7
request: The owner chose 'Fresh sealed sets, then stop': every sealed set of Home, the understanding conversation and the journeys was spent, so nothing the studio changed since could be judged once more.
spec: An independent agent writes each set from the format and the tables only; the file is copied unchanged, its SHA-256 committed, a gate written beside it before any run, and the split wired into its runner so a second run is refused. No set is played here.
plan: Have a fresh agent write each set from a pack of the format and the replicas' or the seeded tables, never the rules or an earlier set.
Check each file's shape against its loader's rules without scoring it.
Pin it, write its gate (the same criteria as the last one, a new version and its own seed) and wire it into the runner.
Make a sealed run ask for --yes even on the free rules arm, since that run spends the set.
Stop before any run: running a set is the owner's choice.

decisions.decision: Each new gate keeps the earlier set's criteria and only gets a new version, split and seed.
decisions.why: Criteria changed after the earlier sets failed would be tuned on what was seen; a new set under the old bar is the honest second reading.

decisions.decision: A sealed conversation or journeys run now needs --yes even for the rules arm.
decisions.why: The rules arm ran at once, so one mistyped command would spend an exam with no model involved.

decisions.decision: Home's runner reads each split's gate and its own runs (gate_for, sealed_runs(split)).
decisions.why: HOME-011 spent the first set; with one fingerprint and one glob, the second set would have read as spent, or a run on it would have been stored under the first gate.

decisions.decision: The journeys set is on seed 7, which joins the lake's evaluation seeds.
decisions.why: Every set is read on tables no earlier set or dev fix used; self-play examples on seed 7 tables leave the lake's train split at its next build.

change: agent_eval/home: requests_sealed_v2.json and sealed_v2.sha256, SEALED, GATE_V2 (home_gate_v2), GATES, gate_for, recorded_fingerprint(split) and sealed_runs(split); the CLI reads its splits. agent_eval/conversation: conversations_sealed_v3.json and sealed_v3.sha256, GATE_V3, an unknown split refused by name, a sealed run asks for --yes. agent_eval/journeys: journeys_sealed_v7.json and sealed_v7.sha256, GATE_V7 (seed 7), the CLI's splits from SEALED, a sealed run asks for --yes after the whole-run and seed refusals. Tests in test_home_eval, test_conversation and test_journeys; harness suite rerun (HRN-077) for the conversation gates' fingerprint.

findings.defect: Home's runner knew one sealed set.
findings.scenario: A second sealed file added to Home: load checked it against the first set's fingerprint and refused it, and sealed_runs found HOME-011, so its one run was refused as already done.
findings.cause: One fingerprint file, one gate and one glob for the sealed split.
findings.fix: A fingerprint, a gate and a run glob per sealed split.

findings.defect: The free rules arm played a sealed set without asking.
findings.scenario: python -m dclab_rnd.agent_eval.conversation --split sealed_v3 typed to see the plan would have played and stored the set, spending it.
findings.cause: Only the reader and team arms, which send model requests, asked for --yes.
findings.fix: Every sealed run of the conversation and the journeys asks for --yes first and prints its plan otherwise.

outcome: Home, the conversation and the journeys each have one unread sealed set, pinned and gated, waiting for the owner's run.
lessons: A runner written for one sealed set has to learn the second set's name everywhere it reads the first: the fingerprint, the gate and the stored runs.
risks: The journeys and Home sets were checked for shape only; a person the engine cannot play shows up only in the one run.
